approval.note: Drafted by the implementing agent. Not approved. Only the user may approve or change thresholds.

scope_note: Synthetic, deterministic windows with hand-written expected alerts. These gates check that the monitors detect the drift they are specified to detect, stay quiet otherwise, point at a real runbook, and write nothing; they say nothing about alert quality on production traffic.

case_agreement.measure: cases whose raised alert set equals the hand-written expectation

false_alerts.measure: alerts raised that no case expected

runbook_coverage.measure: 1 when every raised alert and every policy rule points at an existing runbook with all required sections

insufficient_data_silence.measure: silence cases (too little data, zero baseline) that raise no alert and report the rule as skipped

quiet_window_silence.measure: cases with no expected alert (noise, just-below, improvement) that raise none

real_run_extraction.measure: 1 when a real reference-stack run yields one complete observation (outcome, latency, cost, retrieval count)

monitor_writes.measure: control-store tables whose row count changed while the monitors ran

runtime_unwired.measure: runtime or API modules that import the drift monitors

protected_file_writes.measure: changes to goldens, thresholds, the case index, the runtime prompt, registry contracts, or the manifest during the run

not_measured.production_traffic: windows are synthetic; real alert precision, recall, and the right thresholds need production data
not_measured.alert_delivery: alerts go to an in-memory sink; paging, dashboards, and on-call routing are not built
not_measured.automatic_response: an alert never triggers a rollback or any action; a person follows the runbook
